_: Hand-edited. Everything here changes rarely: what a journey is, who is open when, and which boat goes where. The legs themselves live in legs.csv.
_start_days: Which cutting days a journey runs on, as offsets from the first. '0, 3' is the cut day and again three days later: the barge sails twice a week and everything is built around it. Every journey in the sheet said the same thing, so it lives here and the sheet no longer carries a Start Day row. A journey that ever breaks the pattern can still say so -- a Start Day in the sheet wins over this.
_packed_from: How far ahead of the journey a crop may already have been packed, as the earliest weekday it could have come off the line, keyed by the cut the journey runs on. Cucumbers hold, so a case leaving on the Mon/Tue journeys may have been packed as long ago as the Thursday before, and one leaving on Thu/Fri as long ago as the Tuesday. It widens the day count on the chips only -- the chart draws the legs the sheet gives it, and the sheet does not know which day any particular case was packed. A crop with no entry here is counted from its first step, as everything was before.

sites._: Places we own. They do not gate: we are there when we are there, so they carry no days and no window, and a leg that runs between two of them can never be 'outside hours'. Every place named in steps must appear either here or in hours.

hold._: Test and hold. Each stage is a lane and its hours is how long that stage takes, so the chain draws as a staircase whose steps are the waits; the last stage is where it ends and takes no time. The clock starts when packing ends. A journey picks a recipe by name with its Hold column -- the names are what they are, 6h and 48h, so the sheet and the toggle say the same thing. Branch 2 rows in the sheet are ignored either way.

steps._: The order of the steps is the order of the lanes. A step names the places it runs between; where that depends on the journey, transport or fob overrides it -- fob first, then transport, then the plain pair. An override that has no entry for this journey falls through to the next, so a step can be told apart by island where it needs to be and by vehicle everywhere else. Every place named here needs a row in hours (a gate) or in sites (ours). A step may list what it was called before under was, so renaming one does not have to happen in two places at once. A step marked sticks:next keeps the gap it was written with to the step after it, so that when a later step is pushed it comes along rather than being left to sit. The order here is the fallback; where the sheet names a step, the sheet's row order wins, so the chart's rows are the sheet's rows. A step may name a `row`: two steps that share one draw on the same line of the chart, keeping their own names, their own cells in the sheet and their own bars. Pack/Store 1 and 2 do -- they are the same packing done twice, and two rows made a one-day journey look like it skipped something.
